body.en: The verb is an indispensable part of the sentence. No sentence can be formed without a verb. For this reason, most of English grammar revolves around the verb. Many kinds of questions are asked on the verb in job and admission tests — for example, what a verb is, the kinds of verbs, which verb is which kind, and when which verb form is used.

body.en: The word that expresses doing some work, such as doing, eating, killing, catching, is called a verb. No sentence can be formed without a verb. That is why the verb is an indispensable part of the sentence. A few examples of verbs are: eat, see, catch, walk, etc.

body.en: The word 'finite' comes from the Latin word 'Finitus', which means limited or controlled by another. The verbs that are controlled by their tense and mood and by the person and number of their subject are called finite verbs. A clause must contain one finite verb, for example — He sings a song. He knows it. Finite verbs are again of two kinds: (i) Principal Verb, (ii) Auxiliary Verb.

body.en: The verb in a sentence that has a meaning of its own and can express a complete meaning independently, without the help of any other verb, is called a principal verb. For example — We play cricket. We need some money. Principal verbs can be divided into three kinds: a. Transitive Verb, b. Intransitive Verb, c. Linking Verb.

body.en: A verb that needs no object to complete its meaning — that is, a verb that has no object — is called an intransitive verb. For example — sing, fly, come, go, dance, swim, rise, cry, bark, laugh, arrive, live, sleep, stop, sit, rest, fail, break, close, die, sink, smoke, surrender, open, etc. are intransitive verbs. For example — The girl sings. Bird flies. He cannot swim. The car stopped.

body.en: The verbs that need a complement to express their meaning are called linking verbs, copulative verbs, copular verbs or copulas. They indicate no action or work; instead they establish a relation between their subject and the complement. Some linking verbs are given below: Appear, Look, Sound, Get, Turn, Be, Remain, Stay, Grow, Keep, Become, Seem, Taste, Go, Feel, Smell.

body.en: The verbs that are not controlled by their tense and mood, nor by the person and number of their subject, but cannot express a complete meaning without the help of a finite verb, are called non-finite verbs. For example — He is going to play cricket. He saw the girl dancing. I enjoy watching TV. Non-finite verbs or verbals are of three kinds: (i) Infinitive; (ii) Participle; (iii) Gerund.

body.en: An infinitive is formed by placing 'to' before the base form of a verb, that is, before the present form of the verb. This is called a full infinitive. If the 'to' of a full infinitive is unspoken or omitted, it is called a bare infinitive. For example — Full Infinitive: They want to play cricket. I told him to do the work. Bare Infinitive: They can play cricket. I heard him say this.

body.mix: 1. Verb-এর subject হিসেবে অর্থাৎ noun হিসেবে। যেমন— To tell a lie is a sin. 2. Verb-এর object হিসেবে। যেমন— They want to play. 3. Subjcet-এর complement হিসেবে। যেমন— His plan is to keep the affair secret. 4. Object-এর complement হিসেবে। যেমন— We want you to go there. 5. Be verb-এর পর order বা command বোঝাতে। যেমন– He is to stay here till we come. 5. কিছু adjective-এর পরে। যেমন— He found it impossible to study at home. 6. দুটি clause কে সংযুক্ত করতে। যেমন— He hurried to the house only to find that it was empty. 7. Too+adjective/adverb-এর পর। যেমন— You are too weak to walk. 8. Adjective + enough-এর পর। যেমন— You are weak enough to walk. 9. Enough + noun-এর পর। যেমন— You have enough money to buy a car.
body.en: 1. As the subject of a verb, that is, as a noun. For example — To tell a lie is a sin. 2. As the object of a verb. For example — They want to play. 3. As the complement of the subject. For example — His plan is to keep the affair secret. 4. As the complement of the object. For example — We want you to go there. 5. After a be verb to express an order or command. For example — He is to stay here till we come. 6. After some adjectives. For example — He found it impossible to study at home. 7. To join two clauses. For example — He hurried to the house only to find that it was empty. 8. After too + adjective/adverb. For example — You are too weak to walk. 9. After adjective + enough. For example — You are weak enough to walk. 10. After enough + noun. For example — You have enough money to buy a car.

body.mix: 1. Can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would প্রভৃতি modal-এর পর bare infinitive বসে। যেমন— I can do the work. We must obey our teachers. He will help me. 2. Feel, hear, let, see, make, watch ইত্যাদি verb-এর পরে bare infinitive বসে। যেমন— I saw him go. He let me help him. তবে passive voice এ see, hear, এবং make-এর পরে full infinitive বসে। যেমন— He was seen to go. He was made to do the work. 3. Had better, had rather, had sooner, would rather, would sooner, rather than, sooner than ইত্যাদির পরে bare infinitive বসে। যেমন— You had better go home now. You would rather stay here.
body.en: 1. A bare infinitive is used after modals such as can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would. For example — I can do the work. We must obey our teachers. He will help me. 2. A bare infinitive is used after verbs such as feel, hear, let, see, make, watch. For example — I saw him go. He let me help him. But in the passive voice a full infinitive is used after see, hear and make. For example — He was seen to go. He was made to do the work. 3. A bare infinitive is used after had better, had rather, had sooner, would rather, would sooner, rather than, sooner than, etc. For example — You had better go home now. You would rather stay here.

Feel, hear, let, see, make, watch ইত্যাদি verb-এর পরে bare infinitive বসে। যেমন— I saw him go. He let me help him. তবে passive voice এ see, hear, এবং make-এর পরে full infinitive বসে। যেমন— He was seen to go. He was made to do the work. 3. Had better, had rather, had sooner, would rather, would sooner, rather than, sooner than ইত্যাদির পরে bare infinitive বসে। যেমন— You had better go home now. You would rather stay here।

body.en: The form of a verb that does the work of both a verb and an adjective at the same time is called a participle. Participles are of three kinds: a. Present Participle, b. Past Participle, c. Perfect Participle.

body.mix: Verb-এর present form-এর সাথে ing যুক্ত হয়ে যদি উহা একই সাথে verb এবং adjective-এর কাজ করে তখন তাকে Present Participle বলে।
body.en: When 'ing' is added to the present form of a verb and it does the work of both a verb and an adjective at the same time, it is called a present participle.

body.en: If the past participle form of a verb performs the work of both a verb and an adjective at the same time, it is called a past participle.

body.en: 1. In forming the perfect tense. For example — He has worked hard. He will have passed. 2. As an adjective. For example — Don't sit on the broken chair. 3. In forming the passive voice. For example — A tubewell has been installed.

body.mix: Having-এর পর verb-এর past participle যুক্ত হয়ে যদি তা একই সাথে verb এবং adjective-এর কাজ করে তাকে Perfect Participle বলে। Having eaten rice, she went to bed. Having passed MA, he got a good job. Having finished his study, he went to eat.
body.en: When the past participle of a verb is joined after 'having' and it does the work of both a verb and an adjective at the same time, it is called a perfect participle. Having eaten rice, she went to bed. Having passed MA, he got a good job. Having finished his study, he went to eat.

body.mix: 1. একই subject দ্বারা একটি কাজের পর আরেকটি কাজ সম্পন্ন হলে কাজদ্বয়কে Present participle ব্যবহার করে প্রকাশ করা যায়। যেমন— Eating his dinner he rushed out of the house. কিন্তু এরূপ sentence থেকে পরিষ্কার বোঝা যায় না যে কাজদ্বয় একই সাথে ঘটেছে, নাকি একটির পর আরেকটি ঘটেছে। তাই কাজদ্বয়কে সবচেয়ে সঠিকভাবে প্রকাশ করা যায় Perfect participle ব্যবহারের মাধ্যমে। যেমন— Having eaten his dinner, he rushed out of the house. 2. একই subject দ্বারা একটি কাজের কিছু সময়ের পর আরেকটি কাজ সম্পন্ন হলেও কাজদ্বয়কে Past participle ব্যবহার করে প্রকাশ করা যায়। যেমন— Having failed twice, he did not try again.
body.en: 1. When one action is completed after another by the same subject, the two actions can be expressed by using a present participle. For example — Eating his dinner he rushed out of the house. But from such a sentence it is not clear whether the two actions happened at the same time or one after the other. So the two actions can be expressed most correctly by using a perfect participle. For example — Having eaten his dinner, he rushed out of the house. 2. Even when another action is completed some time after one action by the same subject, the two actions can be expressed by using a perfect participle. For example — Having failed twice, he did not try again.

body.en: When 'ing' is added to a verb and it does the work of both a verb and a noun at the same time, it is called a gerund.
body.bn: Verb-এর সাথে ing যুক্ত হয়ে তা যদি একইসাথে verb এবং noun-এর কাজ করে তবে তাকে gerund বলে।

body.mix: 1. Verb-এর subject রূপে : যেমন— Rising early is a good habit. 2. Transitive verb-এর object রূপে : যেমন— I like playing cricket. 3. Preposition-এর object রূপে : যেমন— He is fond of playing cards. 4. Verb-এর complement রূপে : যেমন— Working is earning. My hobby is gardening. 5. Compound noun-এর অংশরূপে : যেমন— This is my reading room. 6. Nominative absolute গঠনে : যেমন— Walking being a good exercise, I will walk everyday. 7. Possessive-এর পর : যেমন— He does not like my going there. They insisted on Rahim's doing this. 8. Verbal Noun-এর গঠনে : যেমন— The reading of newspaper is a good habit.
body.en: 1. As the subject of a verb. For example — Rising early is a good habit. 2. As the object of a transitive verb. For example — I like playing cricket. 3. As the object of a preposition. For example — He is fond of playing cards. 4. As the complement of a verb. For example — Working is earning. My hobby is gardening. 5. As part of a compound noun. For example — This is my reading room. 6. In forming a nominative absolute. For example — Walking being a good exercise, I will walk everyday. 7. After a possessive. For example — He does not like my going there. They insisted on Rahim's doing this. 8. In forming a verbal noun. For example — The reading of newspaper is a good habit.

body.mix: যেসব intransitive verb সমজাতীয় noun-কে object হিসেবে গ্রহণ করে Transitive Verb রূপে ব্যবহৃত হয় সেসব verb-কে cognate verb বলে। যেমন— Karim ran a race. He slept a sound sleep.
body.en: The intransitive verbs that take a noun of the same kind as their object and are thus used as transitive verbs are called cognate verbs. For example — Karim ran a race. He slept a sound sleep.

body.mix: যে verb-এর subject নিজে কাজ না করে অন্যকে দিয়ে কাজ করায় সে verb-কে Causative Verb বলে। Fell, feed, teach, inform, remind, raise, suckle, lay, show, make, have, get, let, help প্রভৃতি Causative Verb। যেমন— He made me laugh. She had me finish the work.
body.en: The verb whose subject does not do the work himself but gets it done by someone else is called a causative verb. Fell, feed, teach, inform, remind, raise, suckle, lay, show, make, have, get, let, help, etc. are causative verbs. For example — He made me laugh. She had me finish the work.

body.mix: কোনো verb দ্বারা যে idea বা ধারণা প্রকাশ করা হয় তার উপর অধিকতর গুরুত্ব প্রদানের জন্য verb-এর emphatic forms ব্যবহার করা হয়। Do, does, did— এই Auxiliary verb গুলোকে emphatic verb হিসেবে ব্যবহার করা হয়। Verb-এর emphatic forms শুধু present tense এবং past tense- এ ব্যবহার হয়। যেমন— I do help you. He does love you. You did beat the thief.
body.en: To lay greater emphasis on the idea expressed by a verb, the emphatic forms of the verb are used. Do, does, did — these auxiliary verbs are used as emphatic verbs. The emphatic forms of a verb are used only in the present tense and the past tense. For example — I do help you. He does love you. You did beat the thief.

body.mix: Impersonal verb-এর কোনো true subject বা personal subject থাকে না। Impersonal verb যুক্ত বাক্য subject-এর পরিবর্তে সাধারণত impersonal pronoun, যেমন 'it' দিয়ে শুরু হয় এবং এটি আবহাওয়া সম্পর্কে কথা বলার সময় এসব verb ব্যবহৃত হয়। যেমন— It rains in the morning. It snows in the winter.
body.en: An impersonal verb has no true subject or personal subject. A sentence with an impersonal verb usually begins, in place of a subject, with an impersonal pronoun such as 'it', and these verbs are used when talking about the weather. For example — It rains in the morning. It snows in the winter.

body.mix: Inversion of verb-এর অর্থ subject ও verb (সাধারণত operator)-এর স্থান পরিবর্তন। এটা একটি literary expression এবং এটি মূলত গুরুত্ব প্রদানের জন্য ব্যবহৃত হয়। ইংরেজি ভাষায় নিম্নলিখিত ক্ষেত্রে inversion ব্যবহার করা হয়। a. বাক্যের শুরুতে negative adverbial expression যেমন— seldom, rarely, never, little, hardly, scarcely, no sooner, at no time, not until, only + time expression (only when/after/then), not only, not a single প্রভৃতির পরে। যেমন— In no way can he be held responsible. Rarely does he visit me. Seldom have I seen such a beautiful view. Never had I felt so happy. Hardly had I gone there when it started to rain. No sooner had I arrived than the meeting started. b. বাক্যের শুরুতে adverbial expressions of place or direction-এর পরে। যেমন— Round the corner came the postman. On the doorstep was a bunch of flowers.
body.en: Inversion of the verb means changing the positions of the subject and the verb (usually the operator). It is a literary expression and is used mainly to give emphasis. In English, inversion is used in the following cases. a. After a negative adverbial expression at the beginning of the sentence, such as seldom, rarely, never, little, hardly, scarcely, no sooner, at no time, not until, only + time expression (only when/after/then), not only, not a single, etc. For example — In no way can he be held responsible. Rarely does he visit me. Seldom have I seen such a beautiful view. Never had I felt so happy. Hardly had I gone there when it started to rain. No sooner had I arrived than the meeting started. b. After adverbial expressions of place or direction at the beginning of the sentence. For example — Round the corner came the postman. On the doorstep was a bunch of flowers.

explanation.mix: 'write'-এর object আছে (a letter), তাই এটি transitive verb। একই সাথে এটি নিজস্ব অর্থে ব্যবহৃত principal verb-ও বটে, কিন্তু object থাকার কারণে সুনির্দিষ্ট উত্তর transitive verb। Intransitive verb-এর object থাকে না, আর auxiliary verb-এর নিজস্ব অর্থ থাকে না।
explanation.en: 'Write' has an object (a letter), so it is a transitive verb. It is also a principal verb used with a meaning of its own, but because it has an object, the specific answer is transitive verb. An intransitive verb has no object, and an auxiliary verb has no meaning of its own.
explanation.bn: 'write'-এর object আছে (a letter), তাই এটি transitive verb। একই সাথে এটি নিজস্ব অর্থে ব্যবহৃত principal verb-ও বটে, কিন্তু object থাকার কারণে সুনির্দিষ্ট উত্তর transitive verb। Intransitive verb-এর object থাকে না, আর auxiliary verb-এর নিজস্ব অর্থ থাকে না।

explanation.mix: এখানে 'went'-এর পর 'mad' complement হিসেবে বসেছে, যা subject-এর অবস্থা প্রকাশ করে; অর্থ প্রকাশের জন্য complement প্রয়োজন হয় বলে 'went' এখানে copulative (linking) verb। এর কোনো object নেই বলে transitive নয়, আর অন্যকে দিয়ে কাজ করানো হয়নি বলে causative নয়।
explanation.en: Here 'mad' sits after 'went' as a complement, expressing the state of the subject; because a complement is needed to express the meaning, 'went' is a copulative (linking) verb here. It has no object, so it is not transitive, and it is not causative because nobody is made to do the work.
explanation.bn: এখানে 'went'-এর পর 'mad' complement হিসেবে বসেছে, যা subject-এর অবস্থা প্রকাশ করে; অর্থ প্রকাশের জন্য complement প্রয়োজন হয় বলে 'went' এখানে copulative (linking) verb। এর কোনো object নেই বলে transitive নয়, আর অন্যকে দিয়ে কাজ করানো হয়নি বলে causative নয়।

explanation.en: 'To play' is 'to + base form of the verb', that is, a full infinitive. If it were a participle it would be a verb + ing or past participle form, and if it were a gerund, verb + ing would be doing the work of a noun; since 'to + play' is used here, it is an infinitive.

question.en: Fire burns. What kind of verb is 'burn'?
question.bn: Fire burns. 'burn' কোন ধরনের verb—

explanation.mix: 'burns'-এর কোনো object নেই— আগুন নিজে জ্বলছে; verb-কে কি/কাকে দিয়ে প্রশ্ন করলে উত্তর পাওয়া যায় না, তাই এটি intransitive verb। Object থাকলে transitive হতো, আর complement থাকলে linking verb হতো।
explanation.en: 'Burns' has no object — the fire is burning by itself; asking the verb 'what' or 'whom' gives no answer, so it is an intransitive verb. If it had an object it would be transitive, and if it had a complement it would be a linking verb.
